links.outcome: Agreement with expert reference on curated synthetic radiographs, not real-world prevalence data
links.effect: ChatGPT-5 weighted κ = 0.680, 60.9% exact five-grade agreement; authors state results preclude inference of real-world performance without validation on real-world, multicenter, prevalence-based datasets.
links.quote: However, the curated synthetic dataset, limited technical reproducibility of web-based inference, systematic grading tendencies, exploratory nature of the secondary-model analysis, and limited ecological validity preclude any inference of clinical readiness or real-world diagnostic performance without validation on real-world, multicenter, prevalence-based knee radiograph datasets.

links.outcome: Comparison of two AI models against expert consensus
links.effect: Gemini 2.5 Flash weighted κ = 0.23 vs expert reference and 0.06 vs ChatGPT-5; ChatGPT-5 weighted κ = 0.680; Gemini specificity 0%.
links.quote: In the 112-image exploratory subset, Gemini 2.5 Flash showed limited agreement with the expert reference standard (weighted κ = 0.23, MAE = 0.66, exact agreement = 50.0%) and poor agreement with ChatGPT-5 (weighted κ = 0.06).

screen.reason: Evaluates multimodal LLMs (ChatGPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Flash) on a synthetic knee radiograph benchmark for Kellgren-Lawrence grading against human consensus, without testing a deployment practice or organizational safeguard.
